audit.whatIsWrong: Content and full read Graves/Skill/Wukong/Wukong/Graves/Wukong/Wukong; the packet chart reads Skill/Graves/Graves/Graves/Graves/Graves/Skill. Every disputed row is contradicted by the prose directly under it — whys[2] 'owning the short-range trade outright', whys[3] 'you win the extended melee fight', whys[5] 'force every all-in here', whys[6] 'keep it a skill matchup', and mid opens with 'This is your lane.'
audit.why: 55.81% and a page that says 'this is your lane' while the chart concedes levels 3-5 and first item to Wukong. The player reads the chart first.
audit.corrected: All seven rows set to the packet chart, ratings 5/7/7/7/7/7/5.

audit.why: Spikes sit at 2-3, 6, first item and his level 6 — consistent with a bruiser matchup Graves wins on tempo. Collateral Damage's 100/80/60s cooldown is the concrete number the level-6 spike was missing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Graves-side fabrications repeated across the page: 'blind his Crushing Blow strike' / 'blind his strike' / 'the blind eats...' five times — Smoke Screen reduces sight range and slows on impact, it is not a blind; 'twin Quickdraw charges', 'two Quickdraw charges', 'second E charge', 'no dash charge left' — Quickdraw is one dash on 16/15/14/13/12s whose cooldown is lowered by landing basic attacks; 'End of the Line cone' — Q detonates after 1 second or on terrain, the cone belongs to R; and dosFull[2] 'Hold R as the disengage knockback' — Collateral Damage has no displacement in its text.
audit.why: The blind claim is load-bearing here: the page tells the player to fight every extended trade 'as long as you blind his Crushing Blow'. That plan does not exist. What Smoke Screen actually buys is sight denial and an impact slow, which is still good against a gap-closer but has to be played differently.
audit.corrected: All four rewritten to what the Graves kit actually says.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d calls a wasted Nimbus Strike a 'fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.why: enemyKit is null in this brief, so I have no Wukong cooldowns at all. A specific number cannot be justified in either direction, so the invented one was removed rather than replaced.

audit.whatIsWrong: The clone advice is the most useful thing on the page and it is only in early/wants.foe[1]; nothing states how to tell the decoy from the real body.
audit.why: I have no Wukong kit data in this brief, so I will not write a tell I cannot source.
audit.corrected: Left as-is; flagged for the user.

edits.after: Play assassin-marksman: smoke their engage, E through fights for armor, and save the 100-second R to finish, never to chip. Crit carries out-DPS you — picks don't care.

edits.after: Your True Grit stat-stacking and a Quickdraw your autos keep refreshing compound faster than Stone Skin, so you win the extended melee fight.

edits.before: Wukong has only Q at Level 1 and so do you, so nobody owns the first window — just last-hit with the tip of your End of the Line powder trail and stay out of his Crushing Blow range. Once you hit Levels 2-3 you take over: Quickdraw in for the point-blank shell spread, and the key is your Smoke Screen — drop the cloud on him so the blind eats his Crushing Blow strike and any Nimbus Strike auto while you DPS him down inside it. Watch for his clone: Wukong's W vanishes him and sends a decoy walking forward, so if a copy strolls at you, hold your shells and your second E charge instead of blowing the combo into the fake.
edits.after: Wukong has only Q at Level 1 and so do you, so nobody owns the first window — just last-hit with the tip of your End of the Line powder trail and stay out of his Crushing Blow range. Once you hit Levels 2-3 you take over: Quickdraw in for the point-blank shell spread, and the key is your Smoke Screen — the cloud cuts sight range, so drop it on him and he loses track of you while you DPS him down inside it. Watch for his clone: Wukong's W vanishes him and sends a decoy walking forward, so if a copy strolls at you, hold your shells and your one dash instead of blowing the combo into the fake.

edits.before: This is your lane. Your True Grit armor/MR and your two Quickdraw charges (refreshed by landing autos) compound faster than his Stone Skin passive, so you win every extended melee trade as long as you blind his Crushing Blow with Smoke Screen each time. At 6 his only real answer is Cyclone — the spin knockup — so bait it or fight while it's down; the moment the spin ends he's slowed in animation and your End of the Line cone plus point-blank shells plus Collateral Damage delete him. Don't all-in into a fresh clone or while his R is up unless his jungler is tracked, because the knockup airborne stops your Quickdraw and flips the trade.
edits.after: This is your lane. Your True Grit armor/MR and a Quickdraw whose cooldown your own autos keep shortening compound faster than his Stone Skin passive, so you win every extended melee trade as long as Smoke Screen blanks his sight each time. At 6 his only real answer is Cyclone — the spin knockup — so bait it or fight while it's down; the moment the spin ends your End of the Line detonation plus point-blank shells plus a 100-second Collateral Damage delete him. Don't all-in into a fresh clone or while his R is up unless his jungler is tracked, because the airborne stops your Quickdraw and flips the trade.

edits.before: Drop Smoke Screen on him so the blind eats his Crushing Blow strike and Nimbus Strike auto, gutting his trade damage
edits.after: Drop Smoke Screen on him so he loses sight of you mid-trade and the impact slow keeps him off your reload
